title: Good lead trombonists he knew, including Dan Minor and Dickie Wells
summary: He declines to name the best lead trombonist but recalls Dan Minor, Dickie Wells and Henry Coker.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Who was the best lead trombonist you ever worked with?
Oh, that would be hard to say. That would really be hard to say. I don't know. I don't want to do anybody any injustice. That's why I wouldn't say it.
Oh, there's been some very good ones. Some very good ones. Offhand, it's hard for me to recall them all, you know.
Because I imagine some of them might not be so well known, because they often aren't soloists, or at least not what you might call Jazz soloists.

Yeah... See, that's the thing; I can't remember names. I wish I could. In the band with Basie, we had a good lead trombone player, Dan Minor. He's not heard of much. No one ever heard him, but he was with Basie when I was there. Dickie Wells... And Dickie Wells played a lot of lead, too, and that was beautiful. He was a beautiful lead trombone. Henry Coker... Oh, gee, I can't name them, you know...

And as far as records is concerned, then you have to go into another bag, because I don't remember who I played with on records, and there were so many great trombonists who were straight lead men, you know...
